notes.muda: Time as an amount: sina muda (I don’t have time).
notes.omupiira: Literally “ball of the feet”. Often just mpira.
notes.bao: A board game with seeds and rows of holes, played all over East Africa.

guidebook.intro: Football, music and board games fill evenings and weekends across East Africa. Learn to talk about what you enjoy.

tips.title: Ku-: to do, doing
body: The plain form of a verb starts with **ku-**: **kuimba** (to sing), **kuogelea** (to swim), **kuangalia** (to watch). After **ninapenda** it means “-ing”: **Ninapenda kuimba** (I like singing).
**Kucheza** covers playing and dancing: **kucheza mpira** (to play football), **kucheza karata** (to play cards), **kucheza ngoma** (to dance).

culture.title: Simba and Yanga
body: In Dar es Salaam, nearly everyone supports **Simba** or **Young Africans** (Yanga), and the Kariakoo derby stops the city. In Kenya, the big rivalry is **Gor Mahia** against **AFC Leopards**.

culture.title: Bongo flava
body: **Bongo flava** is Tanzanian pop: hip hop, R&B and taarab sung in Swahili. Its stars are famous all over Africa.
